_notes: THE CONTACT BURST, ALONE. earth_contact_8f.png is 1774x887 over 4x2, same
non-dividing sheet shape and the same README-stated boundaries as the rest
of the pack. Explicit rects, for the same reason water's and fire's notes
give.
THE SEQUENCE: c0 the approaching rock with a motion trail (same role as
water's and fire's contact_f0 -- the played layer starts at startFrame 2).
c1 the rock beginning to crack and spark at its tip. c2 the crack widening,
chunks starting to separate. c3 is the WIDEST frame -- 30.7% ink, runner-up
c2 at 24.3% -- the rock broken fully into flying pieces, source frame 4
one-indexed, the same peak position fire's and water's own contact_f3 land
on. c4 continues the scatter (23.3% ink). c5-c7 thin the debris field out;
c7 is nearly empty.
THE README'S OWN WARNING, CONFIRMED RATHER THAN JUST QUOTED: 'Peak impact
approaches the source top edge; inspect for clipped fragments before
finalizing the recipe.' Checked -- BOTH c3 (the peak) and c4 touch the TOP
edge of their own cells, and looking at the composited grid at least one
flying rock fragment in each is visibly cut by the cell's top boundary. This
is baked into the delivered pixels, not an artifact of this recipe's slicing
-- explicit rects do not recover a fragment the source sheet never drew past
its own edge. Reported plainly rather than hidden: the earth impact's
flying debris is measurably and visibly clipped at the top in both of its
two widest frames.
GIVEN THAT CLIP, c3 gets NO hold-and-grow step (unlike fire's and water's
matching hold+scale on their own clean peak frame) -- growing an already
clipped frame about its own centre inside a 444 cell would clip more
fragments, not just add weight. c3 keeps hold: 2 for a beat on the blow
without the extra scale.
CANVAS 512, same headroom reasoning as the rest of the pack.
